This petition has been filed seeking to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.14 of 2019 pending on the file of the learned Special Judicial Magistrate, Special Court for Exclusive Trial of Land Grabbing Cases, Madurai.

sentences.text: 2. The case of the prosecution is that the property situated in S.No.299/1a16 to an extent of 14 cents of land and a rice mill situated in the said survey number by virtue of patta standing in the name of the defacto complainant, the first petitioner transferred the said property in the name of the second petitioner by a settlement deed dated 06.11.2017.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD)No.14240 of 2022
When the same was questioned by the defacto complainant, he was threatened by the petitioners, scolded him using filthy language and also attacked him.

Hence, the second respondent made a complaint before the first respondent Police and the first respondent Police registered a case in Crime No.4 of 20180 against the petitioners and the respondent Police conducted the investigation and on completion of investigation, the charge sheet has been filed before the learned Special Judicial Magistrate, Special Court for Exclusive Trial of Land Grabbing Cases, Madurai and the learned Judicial Magistrate has taken cognizance in C.C.No.14 of 2019 for the alleged offence punishable under Sections 420, 465, 468, 120B, 294(b), 323, 471 of I.P.C as against the petitioners.

entities.text: Special Judicial Magistrate, Special Court for Exclusive Trial of Land Grabbing Cases, Madurai
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3.The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners would submit that a false case has been foisted against the petitioners.
The property in dispute was inherited by the first petitioner by a deed of partition, dated 31.03.1967 among the first petitioner, the defacto complainant and two other brothers.
From the date of partition, the property is in possession and enjoyment of the first petitioner.

Since the patta was wrongly https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD)No.14240 of 2022 mutated in the name of the defacto complainant, taking advantage of the same, the defacto complainant started to claim right over the said property.
Whereas, the second petitioner filed a suit in O.S.No.72 of 2018 for declaration of title before the Munsif Court, Natham and the same is pending till date.
The case is totally civil in nature.
Hence, he prays to allow this petition.

4.The learned Government Advocate (Crl. Side) would submit that there are materials available to proceed with the case as against the petitioners herein and at the threshold, the criminal proceedings cannot be quashed and the charges against the petitioners have to be gone into only at the time of trial and hence, he prayed for dismissal of the petition.

2 5.In the above circumstances, the trial Court has rightly taken the case on file and this Court is of the considered view that no prejudice would be caused to the petitioners, if they are subjected to due trial as sufficient opportunity would be given to the petitioners to put forth their defence.

sentences.text:
The petitioners cannot be let by quashing the charges framed https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD)No.14240 of 2022 against them as that would completely undermine the alleged act,
which is the subject matter of criminal trial pending against them.

Useful reference in this regard can be made to the decision of the Honble Apex Court in State of Haryana  Vs - Bhajan Lal (1992 SCC (Crl.) 426).
6.

7.At this juncture, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners would submit that this Court may consider to dispense with the personal appearance of the petitioners before the Court below.

Taking into consideration the request as made by the learned counsel for the petitioners, the appearance of the petitioners before the trial court is dispensed with except for their appearance for the purpose of receiving the copy of the proceedings u/s.207 Cr.P.C., framing of charges,
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD)No.14240 of 2022 questioning under Section 313 Cr.P.C. and on the day on which judgment is to be pronounced.
However, if for any particular reason, the presence of the petitioners is necessary, the trial Court, at its wisdom, shall direct their appearance on those days.
